findings.claim: `tprod_nonneg` assumes `[L.NeBot]`, but the statement holds for every summation filter, so the hypothesis isn't needed. When `¬L.NeBot`, `tprod_bot` rewrites `∏'[L] i, f i` to `∏ᶠ i, f i`. That finite product is 1 or a product of nonnegative factors, so it is nonnegative. In the non-multipliable branch the proof only uses `tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable`. The sibling lemmas `one_le_tprod` (additive `tsum_nonneg`) and `tprod_le_one` in this file have no `NeBot` assumption and handle the bottom filter case. As written, `tprod_nonneg` can't be used for a general `L` without the extra instance. The multipliable branch also reproves `HasProd.nonneg` inline with `ge_of_tendsto'`/`prod_nonneg` instead of calling the lemma this PR adds just above it.
findings.requested_change:
Remove `[L.NeBot]` from `tprod_nonneg` and add the bottom filter case, following `tprod_le_one` and reusing `HasProd.nonneg`. For example:
```
theorem tprod_nonneg [CommMonoidWithZero α] [TopologicalSpace α] [Preorder α] [ZeroLEOneClass α]
    [PosMulMono α] [ClosedIciTopology α] {f : ι → α} (hf : ∀ i, 0 ≤ f i) :
    0 ≤ ∏'[L] i, f i := by
  by_cases h : Multipliable f L
  · by_cases hL : L.NeBot
    · exact h.hasProd.nonneg hf
    · simp only [tprod_bot hL]
      exact finprod_induction (0 ≤ ·) zero_le_one (fun _ _ ↦ mul_nonneg) hf
  · simp [tprod_eq_one_of_not_multipliable h]
```
Keep `[L.NeBot]` on `HasProd.nonneg`. There it is genuinely needed, because `HasProd f a ⊥` holds for every `a`.

review_notes: The packet has no Mathlib checkout, so I didn't compile anything. I made one request. I compared the new lemmas with the order lemmas in the changed file. `one_le_tprod` and `tprod_le_one` work for any `L` and use `tprod_bot` plus `finprod_induction` when `¬L.NeBot`. In `tprod_nonneg`, the non-multipliable branch doesn't need `NeBot`. Together these show the `[L.NeBot]` on `tprod_nonneg` is an extra assumption, not a design choice, which is why I filed it. In the suggested proof I used `finprod_induction` with `mul_nonneg` instead of `finprod_nonneg`, because I couldn't confirm in the packet that `finprod_nonneg` accepts the same weak typeclasses (Preorder/PosMulMono/ZeroLEOneClass). `finprod_induction` is already used the same way at line 181. Things I checked but didn't file: `HasProd.nonneg` really does need `NeBot`, and its proof is fine. The `[Preorder α]` level of generality is fine. The proof compiles, so `prod_nonneg` accepts it. The names `HasProd.nonneg` and `tprod_nonneg` don't clash with to_additive outputs (`HasSum.nonneg` and `tsum_nonneg` are the additive forms of `one_le` lemmas). Mixing `lemma` and `theorem`, using the binder name `x` instead of `i`, and naming the section `WithZero` (which could be confused with the `WithZero` type) are style preferences. The missing `tprod` positivity extension is a possible follow-up, not a defect.
